crypto/hash.name: hash
crypto/hash.description: Cryptographic hashing (SHA-256) and password verification helper (PBKDF2) using native Web Crypto API.
crypto/hash.aiPromptContext: Use this block when hashing strings, generating cryptographic check-sums, or securely storing and verifying user passwords without bringing in heavy native libraries like bcrypt.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: The plaintext password/string to hash.

parameters.name: salt
parameters.description: Optional hex salt. Will be randomly generated if not provided.

parameters.name: iterations
parameters.description: The PBKDF2 iteration strength parameter.

crypto/jwt-helper.name: jwt-helper
crypto/jwt-helper.description: Lightweight token signing and verification helper using standard Web Crypto API. Zero external dependencies.
crypto/jwt-helper.aiPromptContext: Use this block when you need user authentication tokens or secure request payloads. It runs natively in browsers and Node.js without needing jsonwebtoken or other binary dependencies. Import using: import { sign, verify } from './crypto/jwt-helper.js';

parameters.name: payload
parameters.description: The claims structure to sign.

parameters.name: secret
parameters.description: HMAC secret token key.

parameters.name: options.expiresIn
parameters.description: Expiration duration in seconds.

db/json-db.name: json-db
db/json-db.description: A transactional, file-backed JSON database supporting basic CRUD operations and concurrency safety.
db/json-db.aiPromptContext: Use this block when you need a local, lightweight data persistence solution without the overhead of SQLite or Postgres. Perfect for testing, configuration storage, local AI memory, or single-developer tools. Import using: import { JsonDatabase } from './db/json-db.js';

parameters.name: filepath
parameters.description: The absolute or relative path to the database .json file.

ds/priority-queue.name: priority-queue
ds/priority-queue.description: Binary heap-based Priority Queue supporting customizable sorting comparators.
ds/priority-queue.aiPromptContext: Use this block when implementing search algorithms (like Dijkstra, A*), building rate-limiting queues, scheduler handlers, or resolving event ordering systems where values have weights/priorities.

parameters.name: comparator
parameters.description: A custom sort comparator function (a, b) => a - b. Negative means 'a' has higher priority.

ds/trie.name: trie
ds/trie.description: Trie (prefix tree) structure optimized for string lookup, autocompletion, and prefix checks.
ds/trie.aiPromptContext: Use this block when building search autocompletion suggestions, router matching systems, spell-checking functions, or keyword filtering pools.

math/matrix.name: matrix
math/matrix.description: Matrix mathematics helper supporting transposition, multiplication, determinant, and inversion arithmetic.
math/matrix.aiPromptContext: Use this block when handling data transformations, graphics coordinates mapping, neural network weight modeling, or computational linear equations. Import using: import { Matrix } from './math/matrix.js';

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: 2D array rows and columns values data.

math/vector2d.name: vector2d
math/vector2d.description: A comprehensive 2D mathematical vector physics and geometry class.
math/vector2d.aiPromptContext: Use this block when implementing vector calculation logic, movement physics, boundary collision calculations, interactive UI animations, or spatial layout models. Import using: import { Vector2D } from './math/vector2d.js';

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: X-axis value coordinate.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Y-axis value coordinate.

state/fsm.name: fsm
state/fsm.description: A Finite State Machine (FSM) manager featuring state transitions, guards, side-effect actions, and subscription events.
state/fsm.aiPromptContext: Use this block when you need to manage complex application states, multi-step workflows, or AI agent loop phases. Define clear states, entry/exit actions, and guards to keep transitions predictable.

parameters.name: config.initial
parameters.description: The initial state key.

parameters.name: config.states
parameters.description: Object mapping states to event handlers. Each state can have entry, exit, and on transitions.

parameters.name: config.context
parameters.description: Arbitrary sharing context / payload for guards and actions.

utils/debounce.name: debounce
utils/debounce.description: Creates a debounced version of a function to delay invocation until after wait milliseconds.
utils/debounce.aiPromptContext: Use this block when handling rapid, repetitive events such as search input keystrokes, window resizing, or scroll events to avoid calling heavy handlers too frequently.

parameters.name: func
parameters.description: The function to debounce.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: The delay in milliseconds.

parameters.name: options.immediate
parameters.description: Trigger the function on the leading edge.

web/api-client.name: api-client
web/api-client.description: An advanced REST API request builder supporting middleware-like request and response interceptors.
web/api-client.aiPromptContext: Use this block when building clients for third-party APIs or backends. Easily inject auth headers globally via request interceptors and handle token refresh or custom error codes globally via response interceptors. Import using: import { ApiClient } from './web/api-client.js';

parameters.name: config.baseURL
parameters.description: The base server API endpoint.

parameters.name: config.headers
parameters.description: Default headers to send with every request.

web/fetch-retry.name: fetch-retry
web/fetch-retry.description: A resilient fetch wrapper supporting retries, delay backoff, and request timeouts.
web/fetch-retry.aiPromptContext: Use this block when you need to make HTTP requests that are resilient to temporary network failures or rate limits (returns 5xx status codes). Avoid writing raw fetch loops manually. Import using: import { fetchRetry } from './utils/fetchRetry.js';

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The destination URL for the HTTP request.

parameters.name: options.retries
parameters.description: Maximum number of retries before failing.

parameters.name: options.delay
parameters.description: Base delay for backoff in milliseconds.

parameters.name: options.timeout
parameters.description: Abort request after this timeout in milliseconds.

web/websocket-client.name: websocket-client
web/websocket-client.description: Resilient WebSocket client supporting heartbeat check, auto-reconnection, and buffered message outbox.
web/websocket-client.aiPromptContext: Use this block when building real-time connections (chat apps, dashboard telemetry streams, live notification listeners) that need resilient auto-recovery on unstable mobile or browser networks. Import using: import { ResilientWebSocket } from './web/websocket-client.js';

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The target ws:// or wss:// URL endpoint.

parameters.name: options.reconnectInterval
parameters.description: Starting reconnect delay in milliseconds.

parameters.name: options.heartbeatInterval
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds between ping packets.
